# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

- `restoreDone()`: cancel restore timer; if `_restoreFirings > 0` log 'restore completed at Xms (restore watchdog had fired N×)'.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

- `restoreDone()`: cancel restore timer; if `_restoreFirings > 0` log 'restore completed at Xms (restore watchdog had fired N×)'.

So the restore can also start late: onboarding first (no `_boot` at init), then `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. If I disarm in a post-frame callback at init when `_config == null`, then `_boot()` starts the restore later with the watchdog disarmed — restore wedge silent again.

Better semantics: arm the restore phase not at `firstFrame()`, but lazily — the watchdog's restore phase arms at first frame, but main.dart calls `restoreDone` only... hmm.

Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓
- `_bootRelay()` → add try/finally restoreDone. ✓
- Onboarding path with `_config == null` and no onboarding store (setup form directly): nobody calls restoreDone → spurious breadcrumbs after 10s.

For the setup-form path: restore genuinely never runs, so disarming is correct. But the onboarding-then-restore path: `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. And initState, when `_config == null` (no restore pending post-frame), schedule restoreDone to disarm the frame-armed phase.

Redesign:
- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer, log recovery; do NOT arm restore. (But then how does restore phase get armed in the normal path? `beginRestore()` in `_boot`.)
- `beginRestore()`: `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore)`. Idempotent (if already armed, no-op).
- `restoreDone()`: disarm.

Wait but the original review suggestion said: "cancel on first frame only for the pre-frame threshold, then arm a second, restore-scoped timer". Arming at first frame is what they suggested. But the onboarding false-positive... Actually in the freeze scenario, the restore starts immediately post-frame; the watchdog arms at first frame and restore:env begins basically simultaneously. The 10s threshold with onboarding lasting longer is a false positive.

Hmm, but with cap of 10 and repeat 30s, an onboarding session of >5 min yields up to 10 spurious breadcrumbs then stops. Meh. But actually for `_config == null && onboarding store != null && !seen` → onboarding shows; for `_config == null` otherwise → setup form shows directly. These could last indefinitely (user sits on setup form). Spurious breadcrumbs would accumulate to cap. Not ideal.

Better: use `beginRestore()` explicit API. Sequence in `_boot()`:
```dart
kBootWatchdog.beginRestore(); // at top of try
...
finally { kBootWatchdog.restoreDone(); }
```
And `_bootRelay()` similarly. And for no-restore paths, nothing needed — watchdog simply isn't armed for restore.

But then the reviewer's suggestion "arm a second, restore-scoped timer" at first frame isn't literally followed; instead arming is explicit at restore start. That covers the same diagnosability (restore wedge → breadcrumb) without false positives. Even better actually: `BootSteps.begin('restore:env')` happens at same point.

But there's a race: restore begins in post-frame callback `_boot()`; watchdog arms at beginRestore — same event loop turn. Fine.

Hmm, but what about "first frame then restore wedge" where restore begins but `beginRestore` itself never runs because... no, beginRestore is the first statement.

Decision: use explicit `beginRestore()`/`restoreDone()` pair. Update the watchdog code accordingly:

- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer + recovery log only. `_restoreArmed` guard not needed for arming at first frame.
- `beginRestore()`: if `_restoreArmed` return; `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore);`
- `restoreDone()`: as before.

Update doc comments. Also update the earlier edits I made (firstFrame currently arms restore — change it).

main.dart `_boot()`: add `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore();` as first statement in try, and finally already calls restoreDone. `_bootRelay()`: wrap with try/finally: beginRestore + restoreDone.

Wait — in `_boot()` the finally already added calls restoreDone; need beginRestore added. Let me edit.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Better semantics: arm the restore phase not at `firstFrame()`, but lazily — the watchdog's restore phase arms at first frame, but main.dart calls `restoreDone` only... hmm.

Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓
- `_bootRelay()` → add try/finally restoreDone. ✓
- Onboarding path with `_config == null` and no onboarding store (setup form directly): nobody calls restoreDone → spurious breadcrumbs after 10s.

For the setup-form path: restore genuinely never runs, so disarming is correct. But the onboarding-then-restore path: `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. And initState, when `_config == null` (no restore pending post-frame), schedule restoreDone to disarm the frame-armed phase.

Redesign:
- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer, log recovery; do NOT arm restore. (But then how does restore phase get armed in the normal path? `beginRestore()` in `_boot`.)
- `beginRestore()`: `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore)`. Idempotent (if already armed, no-op).
- `restoreDone()`: disarm.

Wait but the original review suggestion said: "cancel on first frame only for the pre-frame threshold, then arm a second, restore-scoped timer". Arming at first frame is what they suggested. But the onboarding false-positive... Actually in the freeze scenario, the restore starts immediately post-frame; the watchdog arms at first frame and restore:env begins basically simultaneously. The 10s threshold with onboarding lasting longer is a false positive.

Hmm, but with cap of 10 and repeat 30s, an onboarding session of >5 min yields up to 10 spurious breadcrumbs then stops. Meh. But actually for `_config == null && onboarding store != null && !seen` → onboarding shows; for `_config == null` otherwise → setup form shows directly. These could last indefinitely (user sits on setup form). Spurious breadcrumbs would accumulate to cap. Not ideal.

Better: use `beginRestore()` explicit API. Sequence in `_boot()`:
```dart
kBootWatchdog.beginRestore(); // at top of try
...
finally { kBootWatchdog.restoreDone(); }
```
And `_bootRelay()` similarly. And for no-restore paths, nothing needed — watchdog simply isn't armed for restore.

But then the reviewer's suggestion "arm a second, restore-scoped timer" at first frame isn't literally followed; instead arming is explicit at restore start. That covers the same diagnosability (restore wedge → breadcrumb) without false positives. Even better actually: `BootSteps.begin('restore:env')` happens at same point.

But there's a race: restore begins in post-frame callback `_boot()`; watchdog arms at beginRestore — same event loop turn. Fine.

Hmm, but what about "first frame then restore wedge" where restore begins but `beginRestore` itself never runs because... no, beginRestore is the first statement.

Decision: use explicit `beginRestore()`/`restoreDone()` pair. Update the watchdog code accordingly:

- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer + recovery log only. `_restoreArmed` guard not needed for arming at first frame.
- `beginRestore()`: if `_restoreArmed` return; `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore);`
- `restoreDone()`: as before.

Update doc comments. Also update the earlier edits I made (firstFrame currently arms restore — change it).

main.dart `_boot()`: add `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore();` as first statement in try, and finally already calls restoreDone. `_bootRelay()`: wrap with try/finally: beginRestore + restoreDone.

The restore phase should arm explicitly when a restore actually starts (avoids false breadcrumbs while the user sits on onboarding/setup). Let me adjust the watchdog:

**Fix 1 (IMPORTANT, threads 1 & 4):** Give the watchdog a post-frame restore phase. Approach: after `firstFrame()` cancels the pre-frame timer, re-arm a restore-scoped phase: `BootWatchdog.beginRestorePhase(Duration restoreTimeout)` or more generically — arm a second timer `restoreTimeout` (default maybe 10s? make it a parameter / dart-define). If `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` completes... but watchdog doesn't know about steps. Cleaner: watchdog exposes `restoreWatch(RestoreWatch?)`... Let's design:

- `firstFrame()`: cancels pre-frame timer; if not already done, arms a restore-phase timer with `restoreThreshold` (default, say 10s; maybe `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS=`? Keep simpler: constructor param `restoreThreshold` default 10s). When the restore phase timer fires, breadcrumb: "first frame landed but restore:session not completed after Xms; boot steps ...". Re-arm repeat.
- `restoreDone()`: called when restore:session completes — cancels the restore timer.

In main.dart `_boot()`: wrap with `begin`/`mark` already there; add `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` — in a finally? If createOrResumeSession throws, _boot catches in the try — actually the try/catch: on error, should we call restoreDone too to avoid a spurious breadcrumb? If restore errors, app shows error state; watchdog firing might be noise but also possibly diagnostic. Better: call restoreDone in a finally block? The error path already shows an error UI. Hmm — keep simple: call restoreDone after mark, and also on the error path? Let me look at the catch in _boot.

Also note `main.dart` has a `BootSteps.begin('restore:env')` etc. And there might be other boot flows (onboarding path). The watchdog only arms restore phase if... it arms unconditionally after first frame. If onboarding (no restore), restoreDone never called → after 10s a breadcrumb fires falsely. Need to handle: `_BootstrapScreen` is only for the restore path presumably. What about onboarding? Look at main.dart: line 845: "Nothing to restore: onboarding (first launch)". So there are two paths in _BootstrapScreen._boot: restore path and onboarding path. For onboarding, we should call restoreDone too (or not arm the restore phase). Simplest: in _boot, wrap whole body in try/finally calling `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()`. But restoreDone semantics: "restore phase finished (either path)". For onboarding the restore timer never relevant. I'll name it `restoreDone()` and call it in finally of _boot so both paths disarm.

Edge: app backgrounded mid-boot — timer fires while background; that's the "defensible" noise. Fine.

Threshold default: restore includes createOrResumeSession with disk reads; typical < 1s. Default 10s seems safe. Make it a constructor param `restoreThreshold` with default `Duration(seconds: 10)` and dart-define? The PR description mentions threshold dart-define for the pre-frame one. I'll add a define `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS` default 100 for consistency. Hmm, keep scope reasonable but consistent. I'll do constructor param with a static const default from environment, mirroring existing pattern.

Test additions (TDD):
- restore phase: after firstFrame, if restoreThreshold elapses without restoreDone → breadcrumb fires with restore message + boot steps; repeat firing.
- restoreDone before restoreThreshold → no breadcrumb.
- combined: late restore fires recovery line? Maybe log "restore completed at Xms (watchdog had fired N×)" if firings during restore phase. Nice symmetry. Keep: `_restoreFirings` counter; on restoreDone, if >0, breadcrumb 'restore completed at ...'.

**Fix 2 (SUGGESTION, threads 2 & 5):** Document blind spot in class doc — add lines to the `BootWatchdog` doc comment.

**Fix 3 (SUGGESTION, threads 3 & 6):** Bound repeat firing count — cap at e.g. 10 firings with final "giving up" line. Apply cap per phase (pre-frame and restore-phase each capped?). Simplest: a global `_firings` cap of 10 across... The suggestion says stop after 10 firings with a final line. I'll implement `_maxFirings = 10`; when firings reach cap, log "...; watchdog giving up after N firings" and don't re-arm. Counter per watchdog instance shared across phases is fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Good. `_boot` has try/on-Object-catch. I'll wrap restore completion signal via `finally` calling `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()`.

Now implement. Design decisions:

In `BootWatchdog`:
- Add `restoreThreshold` param (default from `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 100).
- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer; arm restore-phase timer `_armRestore(restoreThreshold)`. Log recovery line if pre-frame firings > 0 (existing behavior).
- `restoreDone()`: cancel restore timer; if `_restoreFirings > 0` log 'restore completed at Xms (restore watchdog had fired N×)'.
- `_fireRestore()`: similar breadcrumb: 'restore not completed after Xms (firing #N); boot steps ...'; re-arm repeatInterval; cap.
- Cap: `_maxFirings = 10` per phase? Or total? Suggestion: "stop after 10 firings with a final 'giving up' line". I'll cap each phase at 10 — actually simpler global: firings across both phases share the cap? Cleanest: `_firings` counts pre-frame firings; add `_restoreFirings` capped at `_maxRepeatFirings = 10`. On reaching cap, log giving-up line, don't re-arm.

Wait — also after cap reached in restore phase, no re-arm; restoreDone still fine.

Doc: add blind-spot documentation lines.

Also `firstFrame()` when called by tests: restore timer arms; tests using fakeAsync need restoreDone or elapse... Existing tests call watchdog.firstFrame() then elapse 5 minutes expecting no breadcrumbs — with restore phase armed, the restore timer would fire! Need to update those tests: call `watchdog.restoreDone()` after firstFrame in existing tests, or the "no breadcrumb" test now exercises the restore phase. Existing tests:

- 'the first frame cancels the watchdog without any breadcrumb' — elapses 5 min after firstFrame. With restore phase, firings would occur. Update to call restoreDone() and keep expectation.
- 'a late first frame...' — firstFrame then expects 2 breadcrumbs; add restoreDone.

New tests:
- restore phase fires when restore:session doesn't complete within restoreThreshold (post-frame wedge scenario — the ticket's actual freeze).
- restoreDone before threshold → silent.
- repeat firing and cap at max (e.g. elapse 11*30s → 10 firings + giving-up, then no more).
- late restoreDone logs recovery.

blocks.text:
Now the design for the rework. Three fixes:

**Fix 1 (IMPORTANT, threads 1 & 4):** Give the watchdog a post-frame restore phase. Approach: after `firstFrame()` cancels the pre-frame timer, re-arm a restore-scoped phase: `BootWatchdog.beginRestorePhase(Duration restoreTimeout)` or more generically — arm a second timer `restoreTimeout` (default maybe 10s? make it a parameter / dart-define). If `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` completes... but watchdog doesn't know about steps. Cleaner: watchdog exposes `restoreWatch(RestoreWatch?)`... Let's design:

- `firstFrame()`: cancels pre-frame timer; if not already done, arms a restore-phase timer with `restoreThreshold` (default, say 10s; maybe `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS=`? Keep simpler: constructor param `restoreThreshold` default 10s). When the restore phase timer fires, breadcrumb: "first frame landed but restore:session not completed after Xms; boot steps ...". Re-arm repeat.
- `restoreDone()`: called when restore:session completes — cancels the restore timer.

In main.dart `_boot()`: wrap with `begin`/`mark` already there; add `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` — in a finally? If createOrResumeSession throws, _boot catches in the try — actually the try/catch: on error, should we call restoreDone too to avoid a spurious breadcrumb? If restore errors, app shows error state; watchdog firing might be noise but also possibly diagnostic. Better: call restoreDone in a finally block? The error path already shows an error UI. Hmm — keep simple: call restoreDone after mark, and also on the error path? Let me look at the catch in _boot.

Also note `main.dart` has a `BootSteps.begin('restore:env')` etc. And there might be other boot flows (onboarding path). The watchdog only arms restore phase if... it arms unconditionally after first frame. If onboarding (no restore), restoreDone never called → after 10s a breadcrumb fires falsely. Need to handle: `_BootstrapScreen` is only for the restore path presumably. What about onboarding? Look at main.dart: line 845: "Nothing to restore: onboarding (first launch)". So there are two paths in _BootstrapScreen._boot: restore path and onboarding path. For onboarding, we should call restoreDone too (or not arm the restore phase). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

blocks.text:
Now the design for the rework. Three fixes:

**Fix 1 (IMPORTANT, threads 1 & 4):** Give the watchdog a post-frame restore phase. Approach: after `firstFrame()` cancels the pre-frame timer, re-arm a restore-scoped phase: `BootWatchdog.beginRestorePhase(Duration restoreTimeout)` or more generically — arm a second timer `restoreTimeout` (default maybe 10s? make it a parameter / dart-define). If `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` completes... but watchdog doesn't know about steps. Cleaner: watchdog exposes `restoreWatch(RestoreWatch?)`... Let's design:

- `firstFrame()`: cancels pre-frame timer; if not already done, arms a restore-phase timer with `restoreThreshold` (default, say 10s; maybe `--dart-define=FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS=`? Keep simpler: constructor param `restoreThreshold` default 10s). When the restore phase timer fires, breadcrumb: "first frame landed but restore:session not completed after Xms; boot steps ...". Re-arm repeat.
- `restoreDone()`: called when restore:session completes — cancels the restore timer.

In main.dart `_boot()`: wrap with `begin`/`mark` already there; add `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` after `BootSteps.mark('restore:session')` — in a finally? If createOrResumeSession throws, _boot catches in the try — actually the try/catch: on error, should we call restoreDone too to avoid a spurious breadcrumb? If restore errors, app shows error state; watchdog firing might be noise but also possibly diagnostic. Better: call restoreDone in a finally block? The error path already shows an error UI. Hmm — keep simple: call restoreDone after mark, and also on the error path? Let me look at the catch in _boot.

Also note `main.dart` has a `BootSteps.begin('restore:env')` etc. And there might be other boot flows (onboarding path). The watchdog only arms restore phase if... it arms unconditionally after first frame. If onboarding (no restore), restoreDone never called → after 10s a breadcrumb fires falsely. Need to handle: `_BootstrapScreen` is only for the restore path presumably. What about onboarding? Look at main.dart: line 845: "Nothing to restore: onboarding (first launch)". So there are two paths in _BootstrapScreen._boot: restore path and onboarding path. For onboarding, we should call restoreDone too (or not arm the restore phase). Simplest: in _boot, wrap whole body in try/finally calling `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()`. But restoreDone semantics: "restore phase finished (either path)". For onboarding the restore timer never relevant. I'll name it `restoreDone()` and call it in finally of _boot so both paths disarm.

Edge: app backgrounded mid-boot — timer fires while background; that's the "defensible" noise. Fine.

Threshold default: restore includes createOrResumeSession with disk reads; typical < 1s. Default 10s seems safe. Make it a constructor param `restoreThreshold` with default `Duration(seconds: 10)` and dart-define? The PR description mentions threshold dart-define for the pre-frame one. I'll add a define `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS` default 100 for consistency. Hmm, keep scope reasonable but consistent. I'll do constructor param with a static const default from environment, mirroring existing pattern.

Test additions (TDD):
- restore phase: after firstFrame, if restoreThreshold elapses without restoreDone → breadcrumb fires with restore message + boot steps; repeat firing.
- restoreDone before restoreThreshold → no breadcrumb.
- combined: late restore fires recovery line? Maybe log "restore completed at Xms (watchdog had fired N×)" if firings during restore phase. Nice symmetry. Keep: `_restoreFirings` counter; on restoreDone, if >0, breadcrumb 'restore completed at ...'.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

blocks.text:
So the restore can also start late: onboarding first (no `_boot` at init), then `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. If I disarm in a post-frame callback at init when `_config == null`, then `_boot()` starts the restore later with the watchdog disarmed — restore wedge silent again.

Better semantics: arm the restore phase not at `firstFrame()`, but lazily — the watchdog's restore phase arms at first frame, but main.dart calls `restoreDone` only... hmm.

Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓
- `_bootRelay()` → add try/finally restoreDone. ✓
- Onboarding path with `_config == null` and no onboarding store (setup form directly): nobody calls restoreDone → spurious breadcrumbs after 10s.

For the setup-form path: restore genuinely never runs, so disarming is correct. But the onboarding-then-restore path: `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. And initState, when `_config == null` (no restore pending post-frame), schedule restoreDone to disarm the frame-armed phase.

Redesign:
- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer, log recovery; do NOT arm restore. (But then how does restore phase get armed in the normal path? `beginRestore()` in `_boot`.)
- `beginRestore()`: `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore)`. Idempotent (if already armed, no-op).

Better semantics: arm the restore phase not at `firstFrame()`, but lazily — the watchdog's restore phase arms at first frame, but main.dart calls `restoreDone` only... hmm.

Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓
- `_bootRelay()` → add try/finally restoreDone. ✓
- Onboarding path with `_config == null` and no onboarding store (setup form directly): nobody calls restoreDone → spurious breadcrumbs after 10s.

For the setup-form path: restore genuinely never runs, so disarming is correct. But the onboarding-then-restore path: `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. And initState, when `_config == null` (no restore pending post-frame), schedule restoreDone to disarm the frame-armed phase.

Redesign:
- `firstFrame()`: cancel pre-frame timer, log recovery; do NOT arm restore. (But then how does restore phase get armed in the normal path? `beginRestore()` in `_boot`.)
- `beginRestore()`: `_restoreArmed = true; _arm(restoreThreshold, _fireRestore)`. Idempotent (if already armed, no-op).
- `restoreDone()`: disarm.

```dart
kBootWatchdog.beginRestore(); // at top of try
...
finally { kBootWatchdog.restoreDone(); }
```
And `_bootRelay()` similarly. And for no-restore paths, nothing needed — watchdog simply isn't armed for restore.

blocks.text:
So the restore can also start late: onboarding first (no `_boot` at init), then `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. If I disarm in a post-frame callback at init when `_config == null`, then `_boot()` starts the restore later with the watchdog disarmed — restore wedge silent again.

Better semantics: arm the restore phase not at `firstFrame()`, but lazily — the watchdog's restore phase arms at first frame, but main.dart calls `restoreDone` only... hmm.

Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓
- `_bootRelay()` → add try/finally restoreDone. ✓
- Onboarding path with `_config == null` and no onboarding store (setup form directly): nobody calls restoreDone → spurious breadcrumbs after 10s.

For the setup-form path: restore genuinely never runs, so disarming is correct. But the onboarding-then-restore path: `_onboardingFinished` → `_boot()`. Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. Alternative simpler approach: rename semantics — the restore phase watchdog fires only if neither restoreDone nor a restore-begin signal happened. Actually cleanest: keep the phase armed from firstFrame, and have the boot paths manage it:

- `_boot()` already wraps in try/finally → restoreDone. ✓

Between first frame and onboarding finish, restore watchdog is armed. If the user takes >10s in onboarding, a spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumb fires (once or a few times — up to cap 10 over 5 minutes; user could be in onboarding for minutes!). Then `_boot()` starts, restores, and finally calls restoreDone.

To avoid noise during onboarding: disarm when no restore is pending, re-arm when restore begins. Add an explicit `beginRestore()` on the watchdog: called at the start of `_boot()` (and `_bootRelay`), which (re)arms the restore phase. And initState, when `_config == null` (no restore pending post-frame), schedule restoreDone to disarm the frame-armed phase.

Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.

Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. {"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md"}

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md"}

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md"}
