{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_3.md"}

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.

arguments.content:
# Rework — open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **`restore:*` marks were dead weight (IMPORTANT, 2 threads)** — `firstFrame()` permanently disarmed the watchdog, so the exact TestFlight scenario (post-frame restore wedge, ~3 s uptime) produced zero breadcrumbs. **Fixed** with a real restore phase (see Approach). The PR description's claim now holds.
- 💡 **Blind spot undocumented (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: the library doc now states the watchdog only detects stalls where the event loop still turns; a synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both probe and breadcrumb.
- 💡 **Unbounded repeat firing (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: each phase caps at 10 firings, then a final `giving up after 10 firings …` line and no more timers, so a permanently wedged boot no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics trail every 30 s forever.
- ⚠️ **Scope creep (from the automated review comments, no thread id)** — 100 golden screenshots under `test/integration/screenshots/` (restored deliberately in gh-1444) were deleted by an unrelated WIP auto-save commit on this branch. **Restored all 100** from the merge base; the PR diff is now exactly the watchdog feature (4 files, net vs base).

## Approach

### Restore phase for the post-frame watchdog (`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`)

New API pair, symmetric to the existing pre-frame phase:

- `beginRestore()` — arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s; one breadcrumb per firing plus the `BootSteps.describe()` tail, repeating every 30 s up to the cap).
- `restoreDone()` — disarms; a no-op unless armed, and logs a recovery line if the phase had fired.

The phase is armed **at restore start, not at the first frame**: sessions with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) must not accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens. This was the flaw in a naive "re-arm at `firstFrame()`" implementation.

### Wiring (`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`)

- `_boot()` — `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain; `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` (a failed restore lands on the setup form — no wedge, no noise).
- `_bootRelay()` — the extension-panel SW relay restores the session too, so it gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.
- The `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks now carry their weight: a wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`.

Behavior remains additive-only — the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — restore phase (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone`, `restoreThreshold` + `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`), `_maxFirings` cap with a "giving up" line, blind-spot documentation.
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart` — doc correction (first frame cancels the pre-frame phase; restore phase is separate).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — watchdog restore-phase wiring around `_boot()` and `_bootRelay()`.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 7 new restore-phase tests; 2 existing tests extended for the new phase boundaries.
- `test/integration/screenshots/*.png` — 100 golden screenshots restored (scope-creep revert).

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 16 tests, all PASS:
  - new: post-frame restore wedge breadcrumbs (the reported freeze shape), silent `restoreDone` inside the threshold, no-op disarm when no restore was armed, idempotent `beginRestore`, restore-phase repeat firing, late-restore recovery line, firing cap (`giving up after 10 firings`, then silence forever).
  - updated: first-frame cancellation and late-first-frame recovery now also assert the watchdog is fully silent with no restore armed.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 33/33 PASS; `test/main_bootstrap_test.dart` — 48/48 PASS (with `test/boot/`).
- Full CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): **PENDING — see follow-up comment**.
- `flutter analyze` on touched files: no errors/warnings (only pre-existing `info` lints).

{"content":"Fixed — took option 1, with an explicit arm so non-restore paths stay silent.

`BootWatchdog` now has a **restore phase**: `beginRestore()` arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s) and `restoreDone()` disarms it. If the restore chain (env → session manager → `createOrResumeSession`) wedges after the first frame, the breadcrumb now fires — with the same uptime + `BootSteps.describe()` context — and repeats every 30 s, so the exact TestFlight scenario (~3 s uptime, spinner on screen, post-frame wedge) is diagnosable.

Wiring in `flutter_app/lib/main.dart`:

- `_boot()` calls `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain and `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` — a failed restore disarms too (it lands on the setup form, no wedge).
- `_bootRelay()` (extension-panel SW relay, which restores the session as well) gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.

I deliberately armed the phase at restore start rather than at the first frame: a session with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) would otherwise accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens.

The `restore:*` marks are now load-bearing — a post-frame wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`, so the PR description's claim now holds.

Tests: 7 new restore-phase tests in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` (wedge breadcrumbs, silent completion, no-op disarm, idempotent arm, repeat firing, late-recovery line, firing cap) — 33/33 in `test/boot/` pass.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Documented — added the blind spot to the library doc of `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`:

> Blind spot: the probe is a `Timer` + `addPostFrameCallback`, so it detects stalls where the event loop still turns (an await-chain deadlock or event-loop starvation). A synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both the probe and the breadcrumb — a silent watchdog does not prove a healthy boot.

The class doc also notes the two phases (first frame / restore) so the next triage reads the coverage boundary before trusting a silent watchdog.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Bounded — `_fire()`/`_fireRestore()` now re-arm via `_repeatOrGiveUp()`, which caps each phase at **10 firings** (`_maxFirings`). An 11th firing never happens; instead the watchdog logs a final line:

```
giving up after 10 firings (boot is permanently wedged or the app is backgrounded); boot steps […]
```

… and stops arming timers, so a permanently wedged boot (or an app backgrounded mid-boot) no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics breadcrumb trail every 30 s for the life of the process. Covered by the new `repeat firings are bounded — giving up after the cap` test in `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart`.

{"content":"# Rework — open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **`restore:*` marks were dead weight (IMPORTANT, 2 threads)** — `firstFrame()` permanently disarmed the watchdog, so the exact TestFlight scenario (post-frame restore wedge, ~3 s uptime) produced zero breadcrumbs. **Fixed** with a real restore phase (see Approach). The PR description's claim now holds.
- 💡 **Blind spot undocumented (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: the library doc now states the watchdog only detects stalls where the event loop still turns; a synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both probe and breadcrumb.
- 💡 **Unbounded repeat firing (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: each phase caps at 10 firings, then a final `giving up after 10 firings …` line and no more timers, so a permanently wedged boot no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics trail every 30 s forever.
- ⚠️ **Scope creep (from the automated review comments, no thread id)** — 100 golden screenshots under `test/integration/screenshots/` (restored deliberately in gh-1444) were deleted by an unrelated WIP auto-save commit on this branch. **Restored all 100** from the merge base; the PR diff is now exactly the watchdog feature (4 files, net vs base).

## Approach

### Restore phase for the post-frame watchdog (`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`)

New API pair, symmetric to the existing pre-frame phase:

- `beginRestore()` — arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s; one breadcrumb per firing plus the `BootSteps.describe()` tail, repeating every 30 s up to the cap).
- `restoreDone()` — disarms; a no-op unless armed, and logs a recovery line if the phase had fired.

The phase is armed **at restore start, not at the first frame**: sessions with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) must not accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens. This was the flaw in a naive "re-arm at `firstFrame()`" implementation.

### Wiring (`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`)

- `_boot()` — `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain; `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` (a failed restore lands on the setup form — no wedge, no noise).
- `_bootRelay()` — the extension-panel SW relay restores the session too, so it gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.
- The `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks now carry their weight: a wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`.

Behavior remains additive-only — the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — restore phase (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone`, `restoreThreshold` + `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`), `_maxFirings` cap with a "giving up" line, blind-spot documentation.
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart` — doc correction (first frame cancels the pre-frame phase; restore phase is separate).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — watchdog restore-phase wiring around `_boot()` and `_bootRelay()`.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 7 new restore-phase tests; 2 existing tests extended for the new phase boundaries.
- `test/integration/screenshots/*.png` — 100 golden screenshots restored (scope-creep revert).

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 16 tests, all PASS:
  - new: post-frame restore wedge breadcrumbs (the reported freeze shape), silent `restoreDone` inside the threshold, no-op disarm when no restore was armed, idempotent `beginRestore`, restore-phase repeat firing, late-restore recovery line, firing cap (`giving up after 10 firings`, then silence forever).
  - updated: first-frame cancellation and late-first-frame recovery now also assert the watchdog is fully silent with no restore armed.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 33/33 PASS; `test/main_bootstrap_test.dart` — 48/48 PASS (with `test/boot/`).
- Full CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): **PENDING — see follow-up comment**.
- `flutter analyze` on touched files: no errors/warnings (only pre-existing `info` lints).

{"content":"# Rework — open review threads addressed

## Issues/Notes

- ⚠️ **`restore:*` marks were dead weight (IMPORTANT, 2 threads)** — `firstFrame()` permanently disarmed the watchdog, so the exact TestFlight scenario (post-frame restore wedge, ~3 s uptime) produced zero breadcrumbs. **Fixed** with a real restore phase (see Approach). The PR description's claim now holds.
- 💡 **Blind spot undocumented (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: the library doc now states the watchdog only detects stalls where the event loop still turns; a synchronously blocked main isolate suppresses both probe and breadcrumb.
- 💡 **Unbounded repeat firing (SUGGESTION, 2 threads)** — **Fixed**: each phase caps at 10 firings, then a final `giving up after 10 firings …` line and no more timers, so a permanently wedged boot no longer grows `logs/app.log` / the Crashlytics trail every 30 s forever.
- ⚠️ **Scope creep (from the automated review comments, no thread id)** — 100 golden screenshots under `test/integration/screenshots/` (restored deliberately in gh-1444) were deleted by an unrelated WIP auto-save commit on this branch. **Restored all 100** from the merge base; the PR diff is now exactly the watchdog feature (4 files, net vs base).

## Approach

### Restore phase for the post-frame watchdog (`flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart`)

New API pair, symmetric to the existing pre-frame phase:

- `beginRestore()` — arms a restore-scoped timer (`FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10 s; one breadcrumb per firing plus the `BootSteps.describe()` tail, repeating every 30 s up to the cap).
- `restoreDone()` — disarms; a no-op unless armed, and logs a recovery line if the phase had fired.

The phase is armed **at restore start, not at the first frame**: sessions with no restore ahead (first-launch onboarding, the setup form) must not accumulate spurious "restore not completed" breadcrumbs while the user sits on those screens. This was the flaw in a naive "re-arm at `firstFrame()`" implementation.

### Wiring (`flutter_app/lib/main.dart`)

- `_boot()` — `kBootWatchdog.beginRestore()` as the first statement of the restore chain; `kBootWatchdog.restoreDone()` in a `finally` (a failed restore lands on the setup form — no wedge, no noise).
- `_bootRelay()` — the extension-panel SW relay restores the session too, so it gets the same `beginRestore`/`restoreDone` wrap.
- The `restore:env` / `restore:manager` / `restore:session` marks now carry their weight: a wedge reports e.g. `boot steps [window@…, services@…, restore:env@…] (in flight: restore:session)`.

Behavior remains additive-only — the watchdog never changes boot semantics.

## Files Modified

- `flutter_app/lib/boot/boot_watchdog.dart` — restore phase (`beginRestore`/`restoreDone`, `restoreThreshold` + `FA_BOOT_RESTORE_WATCHDOG_MS`), `_maxFirings` cap with a "giving up" line, blind-spot documentation.
- `flutter_app/lib/boot/app_boot.dart` — doc correction (first frame cancels the pre-frame phase; restore phase is separate).
- `flutter_app/lib/main.dart` — watchdog restore-phase wiring around `_boot()` and `_bootRelay()`.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 7 new restore-phase tests; 2 existing tests extended for the new phase boundaries.
- `test/integration/screenshots/*.png` — 100 golden screenshots restored (scope-creep revert).

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/boot/boot_watchdog_test.dart` — 16 tests, all PASS:
  - new: post-frame restore wedge breadcrumbs (the reported freeze shape), silent `restoreDone` inside the threshold, no-op disarm when no restore was armed, idempotent `beginRestore`, restore-phase repeat firing, late-restore recovery line, firing cap (`giving up after 10 firings`, then silence forever).
  - updated: first-frame cancellation and late-first-frame recovery now also assert the watchdog is fully silent with no restore armed.
- `flutter_app/test/boot/` — 33/33 PASS; `test/main_bootstrap_test.dart` — 48/48 PASS (with `test/boot/`).
- Full CI subset (323 files: non-golden, non-`cli_visual`, `--exclude-tags integration`): **PENDING — see follow-up comment**.
- `flutter analyze` on touched files: no errors/warnings (only pre-existing `info` lints).
